subject: TEST-NUMVAL-C function
notes:
PB250 LANDED — the format was already correct (the printed page was re-rendered, scripts/render-spec-page.py 958 = printed folio 928, and all eight legal shapes trace through BindNumvalCFamily's positional walk); the PARTIAL was owed to (a) the >>COBOL-WORDS interaction with this format's two keywords and (b) four missing test shapes. Both are closed.

(a) THE DEFECT AND ITS ROOT CAUSE. ANYCASE and LOCALE are ISO 8.9 RESERVED words (cite.py --check 8.9 OK on both; neither is in the 8.10 table) and 7.3.10.3 SR3 therefore admits both as the EXISTING word of a >>COBOL-WORDS directive. The directive was applied by ONE mechanism only — the post-lex token retype (CobolWordsRewriter), which can reach a word solely when the lexer makes it a keyword TOKEN — and both of these words are deliberately left as bare IDENTIFIERs so the 15.94.2 / 15.68.2 phrase parses as ordinary space-separated arguments. So the directive was ACCEPTED and SILENTLY INERT in both directions: `EQUATE "LOCALE" WITH "LOCALITY"` then `TEST-NUMVAL-C(X LOCALITY FR)` rejected legal source with a COBOL1504 arity error naming the renamed keyword (measured), and `UNDEFINE "ANYCASE"` still ate the user's own data item as the keyword, switching on case-insensitive currency matching and injecting the compilation-unit currency with no diagnostic (measured: a wrong TEST-NUMVAL-C answer of 1 where 0 is required by 15.94.4 1)a)).

THE FIX IS THE SECOND MECHANISM, ONCE, FOR THE WHOLE CLASS. CobolWordsMap.Resolve is now the ONE reading of 7.3.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 (canonical for an EQUATE/SUBSTITUTE synonym, null for an UNDEFINE'd or SUBSTITUTE'd-away word, the word itself otherwise), and every by-name classifier calls it: IntrinsicBinder.KeywordWordOf — the single funnel through which EVERY section-15 phrase word is read, so TRIM, FIND-STRING, SUBSTITUTE, CONVERT, MODULE-NAME, LENGTH and NUMVAL-C/TEST-NUMVAL-C are all covered by one change — plus the parser's text predicates, the SET-statement locale categories, the ALPHABET coded-set names and CALL ... AS NESTED. CobolWordsRewriter.CanonicalWordOf/TokenIs keep the directive applied to a word EXACTLY once (the retype already re-spells what it reaches). Measured population behind the sweep: of the 552 words in 8.9 union 8.10, 447 were in the token map, 17 are lexed but were invisible to it (a multi-spelling rule publishes no ANTLR literal name) and 88 are no token at all.

TWO SIBLING DEFECTS OF THE SAME MECHANISM, ALSO CLOSED. The token map now resolves multi-spelling keywords by asking the lexer itself, and the de-reserve retype matches the token TEXT so `UNDEFINE "ZERO"` frees ZERO without freeing ZEROS and ZEROES (7.3.10.3 SR3 names one COBOL word). And SR3/SR4's category test could only ask the lexer vocabulary, so it rejected every legal directive naming one of the 31 section-8.10 context-sensitive words this compiler does not tokenize (HEX, CURRENT, LC_ALL, ANUM, BYTE, ACTIVATING, STACK, TOP-LEVEL, UCS-4, UTF-8, UTF-16 and the rest) — a generated 8.10 table now answers it, single-sourced from the spec section and drift-tested against it.

(b) TESTS. The three positive shapes the row owed (argument-1 ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE locale-name-1 ANYCASE) are 2002/pb250_test_numvalc_remaining_shapes, all three verified 0 per 15.94.4 1)a); the stack-exclusion negative under this function's OWN name is negative/pb250-test-numvalc-locale-and-argument2-are-alternatives (15.94.2 + 5.2.6.2, COBOL1504). The >>COBOL-WORDS goldens the row asked for are 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_equate (GR2 synonym for ANYCASE) and 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_undefine (GR3, the user's data item bound as argument-2), with negative/pb250-cobol-words-undefined-keyword-syntax-withdrawn pinning that the withdrawn syntax is no longer available. All eight shapes of the format now have a fixture or a traced derivation, and nothing in the format binds by a rule stated in more than one place.

THE STALE COMMENT the row recorded (IntrinsicBinder.cs, "The LOCALE phrase is the A.4.9 documented non-support") is corrected in the same change set, as is the neighbouring claim that ANYCASE and LOCALE are 8.10 context-sensitive words — they are 8.9 reserved, and the argument-1 exclusion is positional, not a context-sensitivity allowance. EDITIONS unchanged at 2002,2014,2023.
